A urea plant of that scale is a classic reason for SNGPL to run a dedicated named transmission lateral, and the pipeline keeping the legacy 'Dawood Hercules' name after the 2015 ownership change is a naming lag, not a factual error (comparable to sibling row P4138 'MP 59.91-Nandipur Power Plant Gas Pipeline', named for its industrial off-taker rather than the pipeline operator). Classification (transmission, Fuel=Gas) is consistent with this reading -- an industrial supply lateral of 65km at 24in is transmission-scale, not a gathering line. Owner1=SNGPL 100% is plausible and internally consistent (SNGPL is the Punjab transmission/distribution utility; the off-taker owning the plant, not the feeder pipe, is the norm across this roster's industrial-destination rows) but I found no independent source confirming SNGPL ownership of this specific segment either -- all seven ref units for this row (Status/Fuel/PipelineType/Length/Diameter/Location/Owner) came back MISSING_REF and none could be filled with an independently verified, on-point source this session. DUPLICATE CHECK: this is NOT a duplicate of sibling P4157 'Phool Nagar-Dawood Hercules Gas Pipeline' (62.38km/16in) -- it is that line's expected companion 'Loopline' (a second, larger-diameter parallel pipe added to boost capacity on the same corridor), the same pattern seen elsewhere in the roster (Sui-Multan Loopline I/II/III, Qadirpur Gas Loopline, Faisalabad-Malakwal Gas Pipeline II). Slightly longer route length (65.47 vs 62.38 km) for a nominally parallel loopline is unremarkable (loops rarely follow byte-identical alignment). Net verdict: flagging existence as a concern per the scope directive (no independently found source confirms the segment itself), but this reads as a plausible, well-formed real lateral whose sourcing sits in a non-web-indexed SNGPL/OGRA technical document rather than a hallucinated entity -- recommend chasing the primary technical schedule, not deletion.
